page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose server instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz, the system utilizes the x86_64 architecture with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The hardware configuration includes a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed local storage, while offering zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1714.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1617.89. However, multi-core performance is weak, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3812.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3323.04. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read and write speeds of 29.2 GB/sec and 22.26 GB/sec respectively, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested systems. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor, registering at 21.7 GB/sec.

This instance is suitable for workloads that benefit from fast local storage and moderate single-threaded processing, such as static web serving, which achieved a throughput of 6.5 GB/sec. It can handle lightweight LLM inference, generating 112.55 tokens/sec on a small 135M model, though prompt processing speeds remain weak. Due to the weak multi-core and database benchmark results, it is less suited for heavy database operations or highly parallelized computing tasks.

Performance benchmarks show average single-core execution, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1714.0 and static web serving throughput of 6.5 GB/sec.
